priority_classification: correctness/architectural integrity -- highest category in the standing priority order. A real, silent, total loss of two documented FunctionIdentity fact classes (declaration_kind, owner.target/trait_path) between census and the produced engineering graph, for every method/associated-function/trait-impl in any censused Rust codebase -- the majority of real-world function declarations, not an edge case.
gap_discovered_by: Delegated Explore subagent survey, explicitly asked to check all ~10 remaining projection arms (Symbol, Type, FunctionIdentity, FunctionSignature, ControlFlow, DataFlow, State, Effect, Ownership, Concurrency) against their own Identity struct fields for the same silent-drop pattern just fixed for Call. It reported FunctionIdentity.owner.target as the strongest analog (ranked above a lower-severity FunctionSignature candidate: visibility/generics/abi/is_extern, scalar attributes rather than a missing cross-dimension edge). Independently re-verified before any change: read core/src/semantic/function.rs's FunctionOwner/FunctionIdentity struct definitions and doc comments directly, read the real FunctionIdentity projection arm in core/src/graph/engineering_graph.rs (confirmed it reads only scope+symbol.name), and read adapter/src/semantic/rust/mod.rs's handle_impl (lines 1457-1490) directly to confirm the extractor genuinely computes and passes a real, resolved TypeIdentity into owner.target for every method -- not an aspirational/always-None field.
key_finding: FunctionIdentity.declaration_kind (FREE_FUNCTION/INHERENT_METHOD/ASSOCIATED_FUNCTION/TRAIT_METHOD_DECLARATION/TRAIT_DEFAULT_METHOD/TRAIT_IMPLEMENTATION_METHOD) and FunctionIdentity.owner.target (the enclosing impl block's self type, as a real TypeIdentity) are both genuinely populated by the extractor for every non-free-function declaration -- handle_impl computes `target = self.emit_type_identity(scope, &self_type, Some(target_span))`, the exact same call that produces TYPE's own graph node, and passes the identical TypeIdentity into every method's FunctionOwner. The FunctionIdentity graph-projection arm read neither field: no attribute distinguished a free function from a method, and no edge connected a method's FunctionIdentity node to the Type node it was implemented on. A consumer querying "what methods does type Foo have" or "is this an impl of a trait" could not answer that from the graph at all, for the majority of real-world function declarations (anything inside an impl or trait block), despite the extractor already proving and emitting this data on every extraction.
verification_before_acting: Read FunctionOwner/FunctionIdentity's real struct definitions and doc comments in core/src/semantic/function.rs directly -- confirmed target/trait_path/declaration_kind are real, non-optional-in-spirit fields (Option<TypeIdentity> is None only for FreeFunction/TraitMethodDeclaration/TraitDefaultMethod, by the field's own doc comment, not because the extractor fails to populate it).
Read the real FunctionIdentity projection arm in engineering_graph.rs directly (not from the subagent's paraphrase) and confirmed it reads only header.scope and header.subject.symbol.name.

Read adapter/src/semantic/rust/mod.rs's handle_impl (lines 1457-1490) directly to confirm target = self.emit_type_identity(...) is the SAME TypeIdentity-producing call TYPE's own observations use, and that owner.target/trait_path are populated for InherentMethod/AssociatedFunction/TraitImplementationMethod -- not merely claimed by the subagent.

Confirmed TypeIdentity::identity_key() and the SemanticRecordId::new(SemanticDimension::Type, ...) formula used in emit_type_identity (adapter/src/semantic/rust/mod.rs:671) is the exact formula the Type graph arm's own node id already derives from (header.record_id, itself built the same way) -- meaning recomputing SemanticRecordId::new(SemanticDimension::Type, &target.identity_key()) inside the FunctionIdentity arm deterministically reaches the SAME node id TYPE's own observation of that spelling produces, with no new lookup logic needed.

Checked the existing function_identity_observation test helper and discovered it ALREADY sets owner.target to a real, resolved TypeIdentity (used by every existing Call/FunctionIdentity test in this file) -- meaning this fix's new edge is exercised, silently, by essentially every existing test in this file the moment it's added; ran the full core test suite immediately after implementing (before writing any new test) specifically to catch any hidden assumption an existing test might have made about FunctionIdentity nodes having no outgoing edges -- none did (167 passed, unchanged).

design_decisions.question: Which fields to project in this fix -- everything FunctionIdentity carries, or a scoped subset?
design_decisions.decision: declaration_kind (as a new node attribute, cheap and always-real) plus owner.target/trait_path (as a new IMPLEMENTED_ON edge with a trait_path attribute when present) only. Left FunctionIdentity.generics and the separately-flagged, lower-severity FunctionSignature fields (visibility/generics/abi/is_extern) unfixed this generation -- scoped to the single strongest, most-analogous-to-Call candidate rather than bundling multiple unrelated field-projection gaps into one change, consistent with this session's own narrow-fix discipline.

design_decisions.question: Edge kind name and shape for the impl-target relationship?
design_decisions.decision: IMPLEMENTED_ON, one edge per method with a resolved owner.target, from the FunctionIdentity node to the Type node, carrying a trait_path attribute when the method is a trait implementation (owner.trait_path is Some) -- distinct from CALL's BINDS_ARGUMENT/BINDS_RESULT and PERSISTENCE's REFERS_TO_PLACE, matching this file's own convention of one distinct, clearly-named edge kind per distinct relationship.
